agent_note: Third-person present-tense narration following one character, plus an embedded first-person past-tense memoir that the character is writing - the same structural shape as Cloud Cuckoo Land's Aethon strand in the METHODOLOGY validation table. 22 event quotes, 20 present / 2 past = 90.9% present. Both past quotes (q05618, q05621) are the embedded memoir, so the minority is structural rather than noise; at 9% it is well short of the 25% needed for a mixed or dual finding, so I recorded narrating_situation as simultaneous with the embedded strand noted rather than dual. Not in the flagged 70-85% band. NO SINGLE QUOTE FLIPS THIS BOOK: moving any one present quote to past gives 19/22 = 86.4%, still above the 85% bar; it would take two reclassifications to drop below it. The recurring judgment call here is King's 'Billy thinks / he guesses / he doubts X' construction, where a present-tense reporting verb about a specific character introduces a generalization (q05615, q05639, q05644, and less clearly q05637, q05642, q05648). I counted these as event/present because the narrating verb reports a specific character's mental state at a story moment, which is what METHODOLOGY's specificity test asks for. Reading all six as gnomic instead would leave 14 present / 2 past = 87.5%, so even the maximally conservative treatment of this pattern does not change the outcome. 18 of 44 quotes are gnomic - the usual Goodreads aphorism bias - and q05619 is a reading-group guide leaking in from the back matter.
